clue.text: Philosopher's making a record about medicine

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the short phrase before it is read from right to left

parts.note: taken as written
LP is a long-playing record
a tonic is a restorative medicine

explanation.surface: A philosopher cuts an album about a remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Philosopher's' is not a possessive noun but the adjective form, belonging to Plato.
explanation.definitionFit: Platonic describes the ideas of Plato, the Greek thinker, so it means belonging to that philosopher.

clue.text: Lesson I adapted for big game

indicators.note: adapted means changed to fit, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A teacher adapts a lesson for a major sports fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big game' suggests an important match, but means large animals hunted on safari.
explanation.definitionFit: A lioness is a female lion, one of the large wild animals hunters call big game.

clue.text: Receive role in play? Pan

parts.note: to take is to receive
a part is a role in a play

explanation.surface: An actor accepting a role, perhaps as Peter Pan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pan' looks like Peter Pan, a role in a play, but it is a verb: to criticise harshly.
explanation.definitionFit: To pan a show and to take it apart both mean to criticise it severely and in detail.

clue.text: Tree presented by Head Girl

parts.note: nut is slang for the head
a girl's name

explanation.surface: A tree given to the school by the head girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head Girl' reads as one school title, but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The nutmeg is a tropical evergreen whose seed is ground as a spice.

clue.text: Canons hostile about new authority

parts.note: the canons of a cathedral together form its chapter

indicators.note: about means going round, so the hostile word wraps around the next piece

parts.note: averse means opposed
N is the abbreviation for new; no word in the clue as printed gives the D

explanation.surface: Clergy resisting a new authority figure.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay as printed falls one letter short: N comes from new, but nothing supplies the D. Canons here are clergy, not rules.
explanation.definitionFit: Chapter and verse means an exact, authoritative source, as when citing the precise Bible passage.

clue.text: Painful emotion about one pound stake

indicators.note: about means going round, so the painful word wraps around the two short pieces

parts.note: a pang is a sharp twinge of feeling
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Heartache over a pound bet.
explanation.walkthrough: The two letters go inside with the pound first; 'stake' looks like a wager but is a wooden post.
explanation.definitionFit: A paling is a pointed wooden post used in fencing, which is one kind of stake.

clue.text: Standard medical equipment, in a manner of speaking

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level
a lance is a surgical blade, usually lancet

explanation.surface: Normal hospital kit, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a manner of speaking' looks like a stock phrase meaning 'so to speak', but 'in a' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Parlance is a particular way of talking or idiom, such as legal parlance.

clue.text: Picture — one with the speaker holding a drink

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: holding means clasping something inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: the speaker refers to themselves as me
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: A picture of someone at a podium with a drink in hand.
explanation.definitionFit: To picture something in the mind is to imagine or visualise it.

clue.text: Resentful of Dior's lead after New Look

indicators.note: after puts the letter behind the pieces that come later in the clue

parts.note: green means new and inexperienced
to eye is to look at

indicators.note: lead means the front, so only the initial letter of the designer's name is kept

parts.note: first letter of Dior

explanation.surface: Jealous of Dior's success after his famous 1947 collection.
explanation.walkthrough: The New Look was Christian Dior's 1947 fashion line, which makes the two words seem one name.
explanation.definitionFit: Green-eyed means jealous or envious, from Shakespeare's green-eyed monster.

clue.text: Put ingredient for salad dressing down

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the peppery leaf also called arugula
second meaning: British slang for a severe telling-off

explanation.surface: Instructions to put a salad dressing ingredient on the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salad dressing' runs together in the surface, but the split falls after salad; 'dressing down' is a reprimand, and to get a rocket is British for being told off.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocket is a leafy green eaten raw in salads, and in British slang a rocket is a sharp scolding.

clue.text: Dog given outing and drink

parts.note: something aired has been taken out into the open
ale is beer

explanation.surface: A dog is taken out for a walk and then has a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The Airedale is a large terrier breed named after a valley in Yorkshire.

clue.text: After several years, books become corrupt

indicators.note: after places the later piece behind the earlier one in the finished word

parts.note: a decade is a period of ten years
NT is the New Testament, a collection of books

explanation.surface: Over a long stretch of time, accounting records get falsified.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Books' suggests ledgers, but crosswords use it for a set of Bible books.
explanation.definitionFit: Decadent describes morals in decline, which is close to corrupt or degenerate.

clue.text: First part of play about proceedings in court

parts.note: Act One opens a stage play
on means concerning

explanation.surface: The opening scenes of a courtroom drama.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal action is a lawsuit, the formal process brought before a judge.

clue.text: Try it out loud?

indicators.note: out loud tells us to say the letters and hear a different word

parts.note: it is slang for sex appeal, abbreviated SA, and the two letters said aloud make a word

explanation.surface: A prompt to read something aloud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' meaning sex appeal comes from the 1920s film star Clara Bow, the 'It girl'.
explanation.definitionFit: To essay something is a formal verb for attempting it.

clue.text: If all men start off equal, they're different at home

indicators.note: different means changed, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: letters to rearrange

indicators.note: start off picks out the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: first letter of equal

explanation.surface: A paradox about equality: everyone begins equal but differs in private life.
explanation.definitionFit: En famille is a French phrase for being with one's family, informally and at home.

clue.text: Quite distraught. Pericles finds "joy at last"

indicators.note: distraught means deeply upset, so the name is thrown into disorder

parts.note: the name used as letters

indicators.note: at last points at the final letter of the word before it

parts.note: final letter of joy

explanation.surface: A very upset Pericles finally finds happiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Quite as an exclamation of agreement means exactly so, the same as saying precisely.

clue.text: Arouse terror initially in ape

indicators.note: in places the selected letter inside the next word

parts.note: to ape is to imitate

indicators.note: initially points at the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: first letter of terror

explanation.surface: A frightened monkey is stirred up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ape' looks like an animal but is a verb meaning to mimic.
explanation.definitionFit: To stimulate is to excite or rouse something into activity.

clue.text: Had scrap injured in emergency bed

indicators.note: something injured is damaged and out of shape, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone hurt in a fight ends up in a hospital bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The paper prints 'Bad', but the letters only work with an H, so 'Had' must be meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A crash pad is slang for a place to sleep temporarily, a makeshift bed for the night.

clue.text: Trace pot converted into foreign currency

indicators.note: into means placed inside the word that follows
something converted has been changed in form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: pot rearranged
the forint is the currency of Hungary

explanation.surface: Following the trail of a pot of money changed into another currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Converted' suggests changing money, which fits the currency, but it rearranges the pot.
explanation.definitionFit: A footprint is the mark a foot leaves behind, so it is a trace of someone's passage.

clue.text: Watch broadcast from abroad, do

parts.note: an outside broadcast, abroad meaning out of doors
something that will do will serve

explanation.surface: Tuning in to a programme from overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abroad' looks like overseas, but its older sense is outdoors, so this is an outside broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: keeping your eyes on something closely, noting what happens, is both senses of the verb.

clue.text: Routed. I fled the scene of battle

indicators.note: an army routed is scattered in confusion, so these letters are scattered too

parts.note: letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A beaten soldier runs from the battleground.
explanation.definitionFit: A field, as in battlefield, is the open ground where armies fight.

clue.text: Most voluptuous lady overwhelmed by desire

indicators.note: overwhelmed by means engulfed, so the first piece is swallowed inside the second

parts.note: lust is strong desire
a lady is referred to as she

explanation.surface: A curvaceous woman consumed by passion.
explanation.definitionFit: Lush can mean luxuriant and sensual, so the superlative is the most voluptuous.

clue.text: Eat in some catering establishment

indicators.note: in some means part of what follows, so the letters sit inside the phrase

parts.note: letters across the two words

explanation.surface: Having a meal at a restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: To ingest is to take food into the body, a formal way of saying swallow it.

clue.text: Regret absence of one's wife

parts.note: to miss someone is to be sorry they are not there
one, as royalty speaks it, stands for we, and the possessive object form leads to us

explanation.surface: Someone pines for their absent wife.
explanation.walkthrough: The royal 'one' stands for 'we', giving US here.
explanation.definitionFit: Missus is an informal, chiefly British word for a man's spouse.

clue.text: Master to disappear suddenly? Without question

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the first word sits round the second

parts.note: to vanish is to go out of sight at once
QU is the abbreviation for question

explanation.surface: A teacher disappearing without asking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like it means lacking, but here it means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: To master an enemy is to defeat them completely, which is what vanquish means.

clue.text: Bird starts to scratch, pulling up radish plant

parts.note: a lark is a songbird

indicators.note: starts points at the opening letter of each following word

parts.note: first letters of four words

explanation.surface: A bird scratches at the ground and pulls up a radish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Radish plant' reads as one item, but radish only supplies a letter and plant stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Larkspur is a tall garden flower, related to the delphinium.

clue.text: Times editor's rousing leaders that can undo mistakes

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for a noun

parts.note: eras are ages or periods

indicators.note: leaders are the front runners, so take the opening letters of the words

parts.note: first letters of two words

explanation.surface: The Times editor's stirring leading articles are correcting errors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' and 'leaders' suggest the newspaper and its editorials, but Times means ages and leaders means initial letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An eraser is a rubber or similar tool used to remove pencil or ink errors.

clue.text: 18+51+500 — pupil's blinded by this

parts.note: 18 down's answer means watch, and to eye is to watch
LI is the Roman numeral for fifty-one
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

explanation.surface: A sum of numbers that leaves a schoolchild baffled.
explanation.walkthrough: The 18 is a cross-reference: the answer to 18 down, OBSERVE, is replaced by its synonym EYE. 'Pupil' suggests a schoolchild but is the dark centre of the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: When the eyelid closes it covers the dark opening of the eye, cutting off all sight.

clue.text: 19 about to take in suit

indicators.note: about means going round, so the cross-referenced word surrounds the phrase that follows

parts.note: the answer to 19 across, a field of runners, is also called the entry
to eat is to take food in

explanation.surface: A cross-reference about someone taking in a suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 across is FIELD; the field in a race is all its entrants, also called the entry. 'Suit' suggests clothing being taken in by a tailor, but it means a plea.
explanation.definitionFit: A suit, as when a lover presses a suit, is an earnest request or plea, which is an entreaty.
